snippet.title: Wilderness Campaign - (1979) - Apple II - WIN!
snippet.description:
➨ Follow me on Instagram: http://www.instagram.com/vghchannel/ 
➨ Donate: http://paypal.me/vghchannel
 ⇩  Click "SHOW MORE" for details and review

Synergistic Software © 1979 
[Computer] Apple II+
Emulator:  MAME 0.215
Rating: 6/10

A fairly in-depth RPG for its time (circa release in 1979, with ads in magazines and everything. I played it awhile, and it kind of sticks.  It's legitimately pretty fun to play!  My first mistake was paying way too much for mercenaries @ 50 gold.  They ate up my resource too quickly.  

The winning strategy was to get a lot of mules, and also hire hands that help you carry stuff around.  Then you can actually carry a LOT more gold.  Each FIGHTER can only have one weapon and one armor as well...  so once you outfit them with the crossbow and plate armor - you don't need the other weapons/armor.  In any case, visit the temples/ruins/castles to stock up on gold and reveal the Oracle.  Visit the Oracle to get the two most powerful items.  Then visit the Necromancer's castle in the top-left.  If you have the right magic weapon you can take down his shield... and if you have enough strong men (you did find the friendly castle, yes?) you should have enough power to defeat the left over of the Necromancer's guard force.  

It's fun to watch the tower crumple in on itself and achieve victory!  It's a great RPG game, from mid-1979 - in fact, one of first games doing RPG on computers.  It was advertised in magazines long before any mention of Wizardry or Ultima!  So kudos, and worth playing from a historical perspective to be sure!

There is an excellent write-up on CRPG adventure, if you want to learn lots more about it:
http://crpgaddict.blogspot.com/2013/02/game-87-wilderness-campaign-1979.html
